page: Microsoft Azure D8s_v7 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor with an x86_64 architecture. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and is equipped with a 480 MB L3 cache, alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches. It is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, relying instead on remote Premium Storage capabilities.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 support) and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE and AMX_INT8), which accelerate vector and matrix operations. In benchmark evaluations, the D8s_v7 demonstrates strong single-threaded performance, achieving a top-tier result of 36.55 GB/sec in gzip compression and a strong 15.22 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 59.13 GB/sec, while stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is recorded at 9308.24. Memory bandwidth tests show a cached read speed of 689.31 GB/sec, dropping to 95.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write speed of 40.61 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated compute resources, the D8s_v7 is positioned as a general-purpose instance. It is appropriate for workloads such as database operations, static web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference, as evidenced by its 16.48 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and a strong 271.19 tokens per second in text generation for small LLM models. The absence of local storage means users must factor in remote storage performance and costs, but the inclusion of premium storage capabilities ensures compatibility with premium disk options. The instance offers a balanced resource profile for enterprise applications requiring consistent CPU performance.

This x86_64 instance features 8 dedicated vCPUs (4 physical cores), 32.0 GB of RAM, and a 480 MB L3 cache. It lacks local storage and GPUs but supports Premium Storage for remote disks. Performance benchmarks show strong single-threaded capabilities, with gzip compression reaching a top-tier 36.55 GB/sec and small-model LLM text generation achieving a strong 271.19 tokens/sec. Other metrics, such as Redis SET operations (16.48 million ops/sec) and static web serving (17.16 GB/sec), fall into the average range. The D8s_v7 is appropriate for general-purpose workloads, database operations, and web serving where a balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and dedicated compute resources are required.
